Workflow / agent / knowledge

Make repeated work easier to run and easier to trust.

Connect operational workflows and build bounded AI assistance around explicit business rules, permitted evidence, and human review. We make exceptions visible and give the system an accountable operator.

Level 2Choose a capability

The constraint we solve.

Automation fails when triggers, data, permissions, and exception handling are unclear. AI adds a second challenge: a fluent output can still be unsupported. Useful systems need tested rules, quality criteria, monitoring, and a person who owns the decision.

Questions we begin with

  • Which task can be defined well enough to automate or assist?
  • What evidence and quality threshold must exist before the system proposes or takes an action?
  • Who reviews uncertain outputs and owns provider failures or changed business rules?

Who it can support

  • Operations teams coordinating recurring work across approved business systems.
  • Commercial teams preparing research or classification for a human to review.
  • Support and knowledge teams helping people use approved information.

Workflow automation and orchestration

Level 4Inspect the detail

Connect repeated work with explicit rules and visible exceptions. We design automation around stable identifiers, validated APIs, permissions, retries, and a named owner for decisions the system should not make.

Where it is useful

  • Route approved enquiries and synchronize agreed lifecycle fields between systems.
  • Prepare scheduled reports or data refreshes with validation before downstream publication.
  • Coordinate documents, requests, and approvals while keeping important decisions with an owner.
  • A workflow specification with triggers, inputs, business rules, stop conditions, and escalation ownership.
  • An implemented automation with appropriate retries, duplicate prevention, status tracking, and monitoring.
  • A runbook and test record covering failures, credentials, release steps, and routine operational checks.
01

Design the rules and exceptions

Map the normal path, invalid inputs, duplicate events, provider limits, and stop conditions. Agree the owner who can approve or recover uncertain cases.

Research agents and assisted decision workflows

Level 4Inspect the detail

Use AI to organize evidence and prepare a useful next step. We build bounded research workflows with permitted sources, source records, evaluation samples, and human approval before important actions.

Where it is useful

  • Prepare account research summaries for a salesperson to inspect before outreach.
  • Classify incoming requests and propose routing with an owner handling uncertain cases.
  • Create evidence briefs from approved public or internal sources for a market or operations team.
  • An agent specification with allowed sources, tasks, tools, output format, and decision boundaries.
  • A reviewable research pipeline with source-linked records, uncertainty handling, and a representative evaluation set.
  • An operator interface and runbook for approvals, model selection, cost monitoring, and failure recovery.
01

Bound the task

Define what the system may read, infer, call, and propose. Agree source permissions and acceptance criteria; keep decisions outside the supported evidence boundary with a person.

Knowledge assistants and retrieval systems

Level 4Inspect the detail

Help people find and use approved knowledge. We structure retrieval and assistance around document access, citations, update processes, and evaluation so a helpful answer does not become an unsupported decision.

Where it is useful

  • Create an internal assistant for approved policies, process guidance, and product documentation.
  • Help a support team draft source-linked responses that an agent reviews before sending.
  • Explore a controlled local or hosted model approach where operating requirements and resources support it.
  • A knowledge inventory with document ownership, access boundaries, freshness rules, and excluded content.
  • A retrieval and answer interface with agreed citations, uncertainty responses, and escalation paths.
  • An evaluation set, maintenance guide, and review process for content changes, models, and answer quality.
01

Prepare the knowledge boundary

Audit approved material, document access rules, and stale or conflicting sources. Define the questions the assistant should answer and those it should escalate.

The operating handover

  • Workflow or agent specifications with clear rules, inputs, and human decision boundaries.
  • A tested implementation, representative evaluation record, and visible operational exceptions.
  • An operator runbook covering credentials, quality review, monitoring, and recovery.
01

Discover the business context

Understand the customer or user, goal, current process, existing systems, evidence, and practical constraints with the people who own the work.

02

Design the working scope

Map the selected capability, define inputs and outputs, validate platform feasibility, and agree acceptance checks and the human decision boundaries.

03

Build in reviewed increments

Implement the agreed assets, application, workflow, or reporting model. AI may assist research, drafting, and implementation; specialists review the outputs and important decisions.

04

Validate the useful journeys

Test representative normal and failure paths, reconcile the important data, and review the result with the named business owner before release.

05

Hand over and improve

Deliver ownership and operating documentation, review actual usage and evidence, and prioritize the next useful change rather than assuming the first release is final.

Before implementation

  • A bounded task, normal and exception examples, source access, and a named decision owner.
  • Provider API, license, permissions, account-plan, and hosting feasibility reviewed for the scope.
  • Output evaluation criteria, review rules, and a monitoring and recovery process.
Can we begin with one focused capability?

Yes. Discovery identifies a useful scope with clear inputs, deliverables, owners, and acceptance checks. A broader engagement can connect additional capabilities once the first workflow and its dependencies are understood.

Will you work with our existing tools?

We review the existing stack before selecting or replacing a platform. Connections depend on the provider APIs, account plans, permissions, licensing, data quality, and the project scope; they are validated before being promised as part of delivery.

How do human expertise and AI work together?

Specialists own strategy, design, architecture, approved communication, and final business decisions. AI can assist bounded preparation and repeated tasks. Generated work is evaluated against representative examples and reviewed at the agreed points; uncertain cases have a named owner.
